title: Your Psychic Powers and How to Develop Them
author: Hereward Carrington
edition_cited: New York: Dodd, Mead, 1920 (Google scan on archive.org, yourpsychicpowe00carrgoog; the catalogue record carries a 1975 reprint date for the same text)
tradition: Psychical-research popular handbook (spiritualist development circles and aura experiments, non-lineage)
locator_hints: Chapter X, 'The Human Aura': Kilner's screens; 'How to train your psychic sight' (horseshoe magnet in a darkened room, then in daylight, one eye at a time, focus)
Chapter on development for materialisation: 'Early signs and phenomena' (blackness before the eyes with specks of light; Madame d'Esperance on luminous haze seen in a half-darkened room)
Chapters on crystal gazing and clairvoyance (overlap with the western-esoteric stream)
summary: A handbook of self-development exercises by a psychical researcher. The aura chapter summarises Reichenbach and Kilner and then gives a training: in a darkened room study a horseshoe magnet until a faint luminosity appears at the poles and edges; repeat in daylight against a window or a white or dark wall, with one eye at a time, sliding the magnet nearer and farther until a quivering band of mist, compared to heated air over summer fields, appears along its edge. He says this needs an act of will and a special focus that often differs between the two eyes. Elsewhere he lists early signs in sitters developing in the dark, including blackness with dancing specks of light, and quotes a medium on luminous haze visible to all in a half-darkened room.
why_relevant: Step-by-step open-eye exercise for seeing faint luminosity around objects, with viewing conditions that let the reader judge it as a dim-light and focus effect; also brief testimony about lights seen while sitting in darkness.

date_evidence.basis: copyright line in the saved scan, OCR-garbled but legible as 'Copyright, 1920, by Dodd, Mead and Company, Inc.'; the archive.org record shows 1975, a reprint/catalogue year

notes: OCR quality is poor in places. In the preface Carrington says the book states the traditional teachings of spiritualist circles 'dogmatically' and does not necessarily give his own views; so its instructions are reported practice, not his endorsement.
